description: NEW, separately versioned supported-reaction labels for evaluation v2. A SUPPLEMENT keyed by gold case id: it adds exhaustive reaction inventories to four pinned_v1 cases and changes nothing in pinned_v1.json, which stays byte-identical so T-107/T-108/T-109 scoring cannot move. It deliberately lives OUTSIDE src/t2pw/bench/gold/ so no existing reader (goldset.pinned_gold_set_path, or any glob over gold/*.json such as evidence/c122_cohort_candidates.py) can pick it up. Every reaction cites a verbatim quote verified against the EuropePMC full text whose sha256 is recorded per case; verification folds case, whitespace and punctuation exactly like bench.goldset.fold_for_quote.

base_gold.relationship: supplement; case metadata (organism, pathway, forbidden identifiers) is read from pinned_v1 unchanged

completeness_definition: supported_reactions_complete=true means: the whole fetched full text (body, figure legends, methods; the reference list only to read citations) was read and EVERY transformation it states with both a substrate side and a product side named is listed here -- in 'reactions' when it belongs to the requested pathway in the declared scope, in 'off_pathway_reactions' when the paper states it but it belongs to another pathway, an assay, or transport, and in 'summary_statements' when it is an overall multi-step conversion. Statements that name a catalyst but not both sides, covalent enzyme- or carrier-bound states, protein modification and regulation are listed in 'excluded_statements' with the reason. It is a statement about the TARGET PAPER only. Per D-093 it does NOT license calling a retained row invented: an unmatched row is unsupported only when the row-level lineage classifier also finds no external RAG support (see docs/evaluation_v2/README.md).
summary_definition: 'summary_statements' are overall conversions the paper states across several steps (e.g. 'chorismate ... through a seven-enzyme pathway ... to produce DHNA'). A row matching one is classed paper_stated_summary: the paper does say it, so it is not invented, and it is not a correct single reaction either, so it is never a true positive.

participant_roles.defining: the chemistry that makes the reaction what it is; a matched row must carry every defining participant on the correct side
participant_roles.cofactor: a currency co-substrate or co-product the paper names for this step (ATP, NAD(P)H, ...); its absence from a row is reported separately as a missing minor cofactor and never fails the reaction match

PMC12096016.scope: Enterobactin biosynthesis in E. coli as the paper lays it out: the DHB arm (EntC, EntB isochorismatase, EntA) and the assembly arm (EntE adenylation, EntF condensation/cyclization). Carrier-protein loading and EntD phosphopantetheinylation are protein-state changes, not free-metabolite conversions, and are excluded exactly as the D-091 audit excluded ThDP-bound adducts. MenD, the LDH coupled assay, secretion, chelation and uptake are stated but are not the requested pathway (pinned_v1 export_rationale: 'Export must exclude MenD, LDH and the transport mentions').
PMC12096016.audit: Read in full (Introduction, Methods 2.1-2.7, Results and Discussion 3.1-3.5, Conclusions, Supporting-information legend). Enzymes with a stated catalytic role: EntC, EntB (IC domain), EntA, EntE, EntF, EntD, MenD, LDH; TrpE/TrpD are named in a comparison with no substrate or product. Figure 1 legend: '(a) Reactions catalyzed by EntB, EntC, and EntA. (b) Reaction catalyzed by MenD.'

reactions.label: EntC: chorismate <-> isochorismate
reactions.quote: suggesting that the EntC-catalyzed isomerization of chorismate to isochorismate has a relatively low enthalpy change
supporting_quotes: it has previously been reported that the EntC-catalyzed reaction is highly reversible
confirming that the observed heats were indeed due to magnesium-dependent EntC enzymatic activity

reactions.label: EntB isochorismatase: isochorismate -> 2,3-diDHB + pyruvate
reactions.quote: isochorismate is converted to 2,3-dihydro-2,3-dihydroxybenzoate (2,3-diDHB) and pyruvate by EntB isochorismatase activity
supporting_quotes: (ii) the N-terminal isochorismatase (IC) domain of EntB (EC 3.3.2.1)

reactions.label: EntA: 2,3-diDHB -> 2,3-DHB
reactions.quote: the biosynthetic intermediate 2,3-DHB is produced from chorismate by sequential reactions catalyzed by three enzymes: (i) EntC (isochorismate synthase; EC 5.4.4.2), (ii) the N-terminal isochorismatase (IC) domain of EntB (EC 3.3.2.1), and (iii) EntA (2,3-dihydro-2,3-dihydroxybenzoate dehydrogenase; EC 1.3.1.28)
supporting_quotes: EntB may assist in metabolic flux in the direction of 2,3-DHB formation by rapidly converting isochorismate to 2,3-diDHB
reactions.notes: The substrate is named by the enzyme's systematic name and the product by the three-step sequence ending in 2,3-DHB. The redox cofactor is not stated in this paper, so none is listed.

reactions.label: EntE: 2,3-DHB + ATP -> 2,3-dihydroxybenzoyl-AMP
reactions.quote: In the second stage of the pathway, 2,3-DHB is adenylated by EntE (2,3-dihydroxybenzoyl-AMP ligase; EC 6.2.1.71) in an ATP-dependent reaction
reactions.notes: The product is named through 'adenylated' and the enzyme's name. Pyrophosphate is not stated and is not listed.

reactions.label: EntF: activated 2,3-DHB + L-serine -> enterobactin
reactions.quote: Enterobactin production from activated 2,3-DHB then involves three EntF-catalyzed cycles of condensation with L-serine via the formation of non-ribosomal peptide bonds followed by cyclization and product release
reactions.notes: The paper writes the substrate as 'activated 2,3-DHB', reached via EntE adenylation and EntB carrier loading. Because carrier loading is excluded as a protein-bound state, a row that feeds 2,3-DHB or its AMP ester straight into EntF represents the paper's own chemistry and matches. 'serine' is accepted for L-serine because no other stereoisomer is in play in this paper.

supporting_quotes: 2-ketoglutarate (the latter two reagents being MenD co-substrates)
off_pathway_reactions.reason: a competing isochorismate sink used as an assay competitor; menaquinone branch, not enterobactin (pinned_v1 forbidden_identifiers: MenD)

PMC12657337.scope: The paper's own 'MK-7 pathway' module (Fig. 1 divides MK-7 biosynthesis into the MVA pathway, DHNA pathway and MK-7 pathway modules): HepPPS, MenA, UbiE, run in engineered E. coli. The DHNA module is named but no DHNA-forming reaction is stated in the text. Precursor-supply conversions the paper states (Idi, acs) are listed as off-pathway. Two catalysts are B. subtilis-derived genes expressed in E. coli; the reaction organism is E. coli (pinned_v1 export_rationale).
PMC12657337.audit: Read in full to the reference list. Swept for convert|catalyz|methylat|conjugat|produce|yield|to form|isomer and every Men/Idi/ispA/MetK/SAM token. Fig. 1's legend lists MVA-module enzyme names (MvaE, MvaS, MVK, PMK, MVD, ispA, MetK, PoxB) and SAM/SAH as abbreviations only; the figure image is not text and no conversion by them is stated.

reactions.label: HepPPS: FPP -> HepPP
reactions.quote: BsHepPPS encodes heptaprenyl pyrophosphate synthase, which catalyzes the conversion of farnesyl pyrophosphate to heptaprenyl pyrophosphate
supporting_quotes: In this pathway, HepPPS catalyzes the conversion of FPP to heptaprenyl pyrophosphate (HepPP), MenA converts HepPP to DMK-7, and UbiE methylates DMK-7 to yield MK-7

reactions.label: MenA: HepPP + DHNA -> DMK-7
reactions.quote: EcMenA encodes a prenyltransferase that catalyzes the conjugation of heptaprenyl pyrophosphate with DHNA to form demethylmenaquinone
reactions.notes: 'demethylmenaquinone' without a chain length is the paper's own wording for DMK-7 here; DMK-8 is a different congener and does not match.

reactions.label: UbiE: DMK-7 -> MK-7
reactions.quote: BsUbiE encodes a methyltransferase that catalyzes the methylation of demethylmenaquinone to produce MK-7
reactions.notes: The methyl donor is not stated in the text (SAM/SAH appear only in the Fig. 1 abbreviation list), so no cofactor is listed; a row carrying SAM is not penalised. 'vitamin K2' is a class (MK-n) and is deliberately NOT an alias. MenG is retained from pinned_v1 as the menaquinone-specific name of the same C-methyltransferase activity.

off_pathway_reactions.label: Idi: IPP -> FPP (as stated by the paper)
off_pathway_reactions.quote: The enzyme Idi, which converts IPP to farnesyl pyrophosphate (FPP), was crucial for further conversion by HepPPS to form heptaprenyl pyrophosphate (HepPP)
off_pathway_reactions.reason: MVA/precursor-supply module, not the MK-7 module; the paper's own legend calls Idi an IPP isomerase, a paper-internal inconsistency (pinned_v1 notes)

off_pathway_reactions.label: acs: acetate -> acetyl-CoA
off_pathway_reactions.quote: We also overexpressed acetyl-CoA synthetase ( acs ), an enzyme that converts acetate into acetyl-CoA
off_pathway_reactions.reason: central-carbon precursor supply for the MVA module

MvaE, HMG-CoA synthase; MvaS, HMG-CoA reductase; MVK, mevalonate kinase; PMK, phosphomevalonate kinase; and MVD, mevalonate pyrophosphate decarboxylase

the latter overexpressing octaprenyl pyrophosphate synthase

PMC12312563.scope: The free-metabolite transformations of the classical menaquinone pathway stated in the paper, in L. monocytogenes: exactly the MenD step. Adopts the biology of the independent audit docs/pwml_recovery_sprint/PRIORITY2-AUDIT-PMC12312563.md (D-091, biology upheld by D-092), re-verified here against the fetched EuropePMC text rather than 01_source_text.txt. D-092 withdrew the pinned_v1 FLAG because the old scorer charged correctly-attributed cross-paper RAG rows as invented; evaluation v2 answers that with the D-093 three-class lineage split instead of a binary flag.
PMC12312563.audit: Re-measured on the fetched text (47,416 chars): MenD 133; MenA/B/C/E/F/G/H/I 0 each; SEPHCHC 9; isochorismate 9; 2-oxoglutarate 8; ketoglutarate 0; free chorismate 0; SHCHC/OSB/pyruvate/CO2/prenyl 0. Every -ase token in the body: decarboxylase, synthase, protease, polymerase, genase (plus non-words case/decrease/release). Identical to the audit's counts on 01_source_text.txt. Supplementary Fig. S1 is not in the fetched text; the audit's void condition 1 still applies.

reactions.label: MenD: 2-oxoglutarate + isochorismate -> SEPHCHC
reactions.quote: decarboxylation of 2-oxoglutarate produces intermediate I, with subsequent addition of isochorismate generating intermediate II and breakdown to release SEPHCHC
supporting_quotes: the SEPHCHC enzyme activity of Lmo MenD was kinetically characterized with respect to the ThDP cofactor and the two substrates 2-oxoglutarate and isochorismate
reactions.notes: CO2 is implied by decarboxylation but never named, so it is not listed; a row carrying CO2 still matches.

excluded_statements.reason: covalent ThDP-bound adduct: internal mechanism of R1 (pinned_v1 forbidden_identifiers: intermediate I/II, placeholder_product)

excluded_statements.quote: enabling proton abstraction and formation of the activated ThDP ylide

excluded_statements.reason: DHNA inhibition: regulation, not a transformation

PMC12421875.scope: The classical menaquinone pathway as the paper states it for L. lactis: the seven DHNA-forming steps (MenF, MenD, MenH, MenC, MenE, MenB, MenI -- the last five stated through the steady-state model's letter-assigned intermediates, equations 5-11) plus MenA and MenG. The L. plantarum biosensor chemistry and DHNA efflux are stated but are an assay and a transport.
PMC12421875.audit: Read in full to REFERENCES, including the Methods model section. 2-oxoglutarate/ketoglutarate, pyruvate, CO2, ATP, SAM, shikimate, DAHP, cytochrome and heme all occur 0 times; 'CoA' occurs only inside OSB-CoA/DHNA-CoA. MenG occurs once. Model 2's chorismate supply J0 is a source term with no enzyme or substrate.

reactions.label: MenF: chorismate <-> isochorismate
reactions.quote: The enzyme MenF catalyzes a reversible reaction converting chorismate (A) to isochorismate (B)

reactions.label: MenD: isochorismate -> SEPHCHC
reactions.quote: MenD facilitates the conversion of isochorismate (B) to 2-succinyl-5-enolpyruvyl-6-hydroxy-3-cyclohexene-1-carboxylate (SEPHCHC, C)
reactions.notes: 2-oxoglutarate is never named in this paper, so it is not a signature input; a row carrying it still matches.

reactions.label: MenH: SEPHCHC -> SHCHC
reactions.quote: We simplified notation by assigning capital letters to intermediates in the pathway as follows: A for chorismate, B for isochorismate, C for SEPHCHC, D for SHCHC, E for OSB, F for OSB-CoA, and G for DHNA-CoA
supporting_quotes: d [ D ] d t = k c a t H [ M e n H ] [ C ] K M H + [ C ]
stands for MenH, MenC, MenE, MenB, and MenI, respectively
reactions.notes: Stated through the model: equation (7) makes D (SHCHC) the product of the MenH rate law acting on C (SEPHCHC).

reactions.label: MenC: SHCHC -> OSB
reactions.quote: d [ E ] d t = k c a t C [ M e n C ] [ D ] K M C + [ D ]
supporting_quotes: The o-succinylbenzoate synthase MenC catalyzes one of the intermediate reactions
reactions.notes: Equation (8): E (OSB) is produced by the MenC rate law acting on D (SHCHC).

reactions.label: MenE: OSB -> OSB-CoA
reactions.quote: d [ F ] d t = k c a t E [ M e n E ] [ E ] K M E + [ E ]
reactions.notes: Equation (9). CoA and ATP are not named in this paper and are not listed.

reactions.label: MenB: OSB-CoA -> DHNA-CoA
reactions.quote: d [ G ] d t = k c a t B [ M e n B ] [ F ] K M B + [ F ]

reactions.label: MenI: DHNA-CoA -> DHNA
reactions.quote: d [ D H N A ] i n d t = k c a t I [ M e n I ] [ G ] K M I + [ G ]
supporting_quotes: MK biosynthesis starts from chorismate and proceeds through a seven-enzyme pathway consisting of MenF, MenD, MenH, MenC, MenE, MenB, and MenI to produce DHNA

reactions.label: MenA: DHNA + prenyl diphosphate -> DMK
reactions.quote: MenA joins DHNA and prenyl diphosphate to produce demethylmenaquinone (DMK)

reactions.label: MenG: DMK -> MK
reactions.quote: MenG demethylates DMK to generate MK
reactions.notes: The paper's verb is wrong (MenG methylates), but the substrate/product pair it states, DMK -> MK, is the correct direction; the pair is what is scored. No chain length is stated, so MK-8/MK-9 are congeners that do not match.

off_pathway_reactions.quote: L. plantarum uses DHNA to reduce Fe 3+ to Fe 2+ through extracellular electron transfer
